title: Minority Collective Action for User-Side Fairness
venue: ACM Conference on Equity and Access in Algorithms, Mechanisms, and Optimization (EAAMO)
abstract: Machine learning models often preserve biases present in training data, leading to unfair treatment of certain minority groups. Despite an array of existing firm-side bias-mitigation techniques, these methods typically incur utility costs and require organizational buy-in. Recognizing that many models rely on user-contributed data, end-users can induce fairness through the framework of Algorithmic Collective Action. In this setting, a coordinated minority group strategically relabels its own data to enhance fairness without altering the firm’s training process. We design practical, model-agnostic, minority-only collective-action methods and validate them on real-world datasets. Our findings show that a subgroup of the minority can substantially reduce unfairness with little impact on overall prediction error.

claims.text: For a deterministic Bayes classifier, perfect success of a minority collective under signal erasure is equivalent to almost-sure minority-focused counterfactual fairness.

In a 4-Gaussian mixture model setting with separable clusters, gradient descent ERM with logistic loss converges to the spurious majority direction yielding an asymptotic EqOd violation approaching 0.5 regardless of minority relabeling.
When the collective predicts counterfactual labels via an algorithm with label error rate rho < 1/2, the lower bound on collective success scales inversely with (1 - 2*rho).

Under Gaussian mixture settings where the minority and majority mean inner product is negative, fair representation learning via projection achieves an asymptotic 1-NN counterfactual classification error strictly lower than 1-NN on raw features.
Increasing the minority collective size alpha decreases the lowest achievable EqOd violation across evaluated datasets until saturating around alpha = 0.3.
The proposed minority scoring methods (RB-prob, RB-label, RB-dist) achieve a given level of EqOd violation with fewer label flips than a random relabeling baseline.
Restricting RB-prob to 10 majority samples yields a Pareto front between error and EqOd comparable to that obtained with full majority knowledge.
RB-prob does not achieve zero EqOd violation on the evaluated benchmark datasets.
Applying FARE representation learning before computing KNN for RB-dist dominates the Pareto front of RB-dist computed on untransformed features.

limitations.text: Existing firm-side bias-mitigation techniques typically incur utility costs and require organizational buy-in.
Prior theoretical work on algorithmic collective action lacks empirical evaluation.
True counterfactual fairness cannot be directly computed or evaluated on the benchmark datasets, requiring surrogate group fairness metrics.
Minority-only algorithmic collective action cannot generally achieve zero EqOd violation under ERM training.
Flipping labels beyond a certain number M increases EqOd, shifting unfairness from the minority to the majority.
The collective modifies only labels and does not alter features, which can fail if counterfactual labels rely on features that are disjoint between groups due to distribution shift.

future_work.text: Study settings where minority features and counterfactual majority features are disjoint to determine when it is beneficial for the collective to modify features in addition to labels.

methodologies.name: Rank by probability (RB-prob)
methodologies.description: Scores minority individuals using predicted positive label probabilities from a regressor trained exclusively on majority-group training data, flipping the top M scored members from 0 to 1.
conditions: Gradient boosted decision tree classifier trained on the modified dataset
Evaluation on held-out test split without collective action

methodologies.name: Rank by label (RB-label)
methodologies.description: Ranks minority candidates by the count of positive labels among their k-nearest majority neighbors in Euclidean space, flipping the top M candidates from 0 to 1.
conditions: Neighborhood size k tuned on 15% validation split

methodologies.name: Rank by distance (RB-dist)
methodologies.description: Ranks minority candidates by the negative mean Euclidean distance to their k-nearest positive-labeled majority neighbors, flipping the top M candidates from 0 to 1.
conditions: Neighborhood size k tuned on 15% validation split
Euclidean L2 distance or transformed FARE representation space
